quizzes.title: Case for Replacing MGNREGA
quizzes.passage:
The Viksit Bharat G RAM G Bill 2025 was brought forward to replace MGNREGA, the rural employment law that has shaped rural work for many years. The government has circulated the bill to members of Parliament. It describes the bill as a framework for rural development aligned with a national vision, and says the bill aims to boost rural employment, promote durable asset creation and align development with infrastructure-led growth.

The government's case for change rests on the argument that the older framework is now outdated. It points to major transformations in the rural economy, in livelihoods and in employment patterns since the earlier law was enacted. These shifts, the government says, make the older design a poor fit for present conditions. Critics have also questioned the quality of the assets created under the scheme.

The bill also changes how the programme is funded. Under the earlier model, funding was open-ended and mostly drawn from one level of government. The new framework uses a shared arrangement, and normative allocations are expected to improve fiscal management and targeted spending.

Labour shortages during sowing and harvest seasons form part of the rural context behind the change. The bill also adds a digital layer to oversight, with a planned digital ecosystem meant to reduce leakages, improve transparency and track work effectively.

questions.q: Criticism of MGNREGA concerned the creation of which kind of assets?
questions.explanation: The booklet records criticism over the creation of low-utility or non-durable assets under MGNREGA.

questions.q: How is the Viksit Bharat G RAM G Bill's scheme classified?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the bill as creating a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with shared financial responsibility.

questions.q: Which group reports labour shortages during sowing and harvest seasons?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that farmers report labour shortages during sowing and harvest seasons.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The bill is framed under the national vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.
Reason (R): The bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha to replace MGNREGA.
Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are supported by the booklet, but introduction in the Lok Sabha does not explain the national-vision framing.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Digital technologies under the bill   ->   C. Prepared by Gram Panchayats
II. Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans   ->   A. Recommendations on financial allocation
III. Central and State Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Councils   ->   D. Review, monitor and advise
IV. National and State Steering Committees   ->   B. Biometric authentication
questions.explanation: The booklet links digital technologies with biometric authentication, VGPPs with Gram Panchayat preparation, the Councils with review and monitoring, and the Steering Committees with financial recommendations.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the bill:
I. Under the bill, the grading of panchayats is based on development indicators.
II. Higher allocations are given to underperforming panchayats to reduce regional disparities.
III. Panchayats are graded on the basis of their population size.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The booklet says grading uses development indicators, not population size, and higher allocations go to underperforming panchayats.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the bill's transparency and oversight measures are correct?
The bill mandates AI-based fraud detection.
The bill provides for real-time MIS dashboards.
The bill makes stronger social audits optional.
The bill includes GPS or mobile-based monitoring.
questions.explanation: Fraud detection, MIS dashboards and GPS or mobile monitoring are listed, while the booklet lists stronger social audits, not optional ones.

quizzes.title: MGNREGA and the Proposed Bill
quizzes.passage:
The Viksit Bharat G RAM G Bill 2025 proposes a new rural employment framework in place of MGNREGA. The booklet compares the two frameworks on six features: guaranteed workdays, wage funding, nature of the right, budgeting approach, operating period and payment frequency.

On guaranteed workdays, the proposed bill raises the statutory guarantee for each rural household. On wage funding, the earlier model placed most of the cost on one level of government, while the new bill introduces a shared arrangement for most states.

The two frameworks also differ in how the guarantee is framed and in how work is planned. Under the earlier scheme, planning followed the demand for work reported by states. The proposed bill, by contrast, sets an allocation in advance for each state and allows work to be paused in busy agricultural periods. The booklet also notes that the proposed bill mandates a digital ecosystem to reduce leakages.

Payment timing also differs. The earlier law set a deadline for paying wages after work was completed, and the new bill sets out a different pattern aimed at improving the cash flow of workers. Overall, the booklet presents the proposed bill as an upgrade that fixes structural weaknesses while enhancing employment, transparency, planning and accountability.

questions.q: Under MGNREGA, what share of the unskilled labour wage cost did the Centre bear?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that under MGNREGA the central government bore 100% of the cost of unskilled labour wages.

questions.q: What term does the booklet use for the nature of the proposed bill's entitlement?
questions.explanation: The booklet calls the proposed entitlement a schematic entitlement, with the guarantee limited by a fixed budget cap.

questions.q: Under the proposed bill, who determines the fixed state-wise annual funding allocation?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Centre will determine a fixed, state-wise annual funding allocation.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The proposed bill's statutory guarantee is limited by a fixed budget cap.
Reason (R): The proposed bill envisages paying wages weekly to improve workers' cash flow.
Which one of the following is correct?
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but weekly wage payment does not explain the fixed budget cap.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Budgeting approach under MGNREGA   ->   B. Continuous operation without seasonal pauses
II. Operating period under MGNREGA   ->   D. Fixed state-wise annual allocation
III. Nature of right under MGNREGA   ->   A. Labour budget reflecting actual demand for work
IV. Budgeting approach under the proposed bill   ->   C. Justiciable right
questions.explanation: MGNREGA budgeting follows a labour budget, its operating period is continuous, its right is justiciable, and the bill uses a fixed state-wise allocation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the two frameworks:
I. Under MGNREGA, the Centre bore the full cost of unskilled wages.
II. The proposed bill describes the entitlement as a justiciable right that citizens can enforce in court.
III. The proposed bill envisages paying wages weekly.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the booklet calls the proposed entitlement schematic, not justiciable.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the two frameworks are correct?
Under MGNREGA, funding was based on a labour budget reflecting actual demand for work.
The proposed bill's statutory guarantee is limited by a fixed budget cap.
Under MGNREGA, the operating period was designed to be continuous.
Under the proposed bill, citizens can sue the government if work is denied.
questions.explanation: The first three statements match the booklet, while the proposed bill's entitlement is schematic, so citizens cannot sue under it.

questions.q: What term does the booklet use for the nature of the proposed bill's entitlement? (one word)

questions.q: Under MGNREGA, funding was based on a budget reflecting actual demand for work. What is the word that precedes budget in this term? (one word)
